title: Learned clinical and genetic features classify radiation pneumonitis in a small cohort
summary: Learned feature selection and classifiers evaluated radiation-pneumonitis outcomes in 59 lung-cancer patients. A four-variable set combining clinical, treatment-volume and genetic information yielded a reported XGBoost AUC of 0.815 in repeated internal evaluation. This is exploratory cohort validation, without an independently tested pretreatment risk tool or demonstrated treatment benefit.
ai_technology: LASSO; recursive feature elimination; XGBoost; random forest; support-vector machine

evidence.tested: Prospectively collected 2017-2019 cohort data were analyzed using internal nested cross-validation and training-fold oversampling. The endpoint was grade2-or-higher radiation pneumonitis, occurring in about20% of59 patients.
evidence.unknown: Prospective collection does not establish a locked prospective predictor. Final features were aggregated across folds before another evaluation, so full selection-pipeline isolation is not established. Model/feature-set choice reused the same small cohort; no external or cross-ethnicity validation, causal genetic mechanism or clinical benefit was demonstrated. Supplementary details and operational laboratory procedures were not independently reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Learned regularized feature selection and classifiers link measured clinical/genetic inputs to recorded pneumonitis outcomes, supporting the bounded retrospective evaluation.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front, clinical cohort/endpoint, computational feature-selection/classifier Methods, Results and limitations; operational genotyping procedures not inspected
